support_julia: Hey team — customer_tom hitting repeated SSE disconnects and partial responses from /v1/streams. They say final tokens are missing and client reconnects then get billed twice. Paste of runtime logs below and a repro. Can someone triage?

customer_tom: Repro from our side: Chrome + EventSource polyfill. Long responses (~40s) start coming through then connection dies mid-chunk. We see `event: data` lines, then nothing. Client reconnects and the server sends the remainder as a new response (so we get double billing).

support_julia: Key bits from runtime logs (sanitized):

```
2026-03-15T18:07:05Z runtime: stream-start id=abc123 client=tom_inc
2026-03-15T18:07:46Z runtime: write error id=abc123 err="write tcp 10.0.0.5:443->10.0.1.8:56789: write: EAGAIN"
2026-03-15T18:07:46Z runtime: aborting stream id=abc123 reason="write-timeout"
2026-03-15T18:07:46Z billing: record partial_usage id=abc123 tokens=842
```

sre_matt: EAGAIN on write + immediate abort suggests server-side socket send buffer filled and write was nonblocking but couldn't make progress. Runtime's write deadline likely fired and then we abort. Can you confirm nginx/proxy in front and whether proxy buffering is on? :thinking:

customer_tom: We're using CloudFront -> ALB -> Nginx (our edge) -> cluster. Nginx configured with proxy_buffering on by default. We tried toggling keepalive but didn't dig deeper.

eng_lucy: Two common places to choke: (1) client reading slowly (browser or network) which fills kernel buffers; (2) intermediate proxy buffering + its read timeouts that cause upstream writes to block. Also runtime may chunk large blocks (e.g., >16KB) and then a slow consumer means those stay in kernel queue.

support_julia: Repro steps the customer provided (they simulate slow consumer):

```
# quick curl reproduce (will show partial and then drop)
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?prompt=long"
```

# node script: read data slowly to simulate backpressure
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async ()=>{
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?prompt=long', {headers:{Authorization:`Bearer ${process.env.T}`}})
  const reader = res.body.getReader();
  while(true){
    const {value, done} = await reader.read();
    if(done) break;
    process.stdout.write(value);
    // slow consumer: pause between chunks
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 500));
  }
})();
```

sre_matt: Thanks — that node script will reproduce. Immediate mitigations to test for customer:
- Turn off proxy buffering in nginx: `proxy_buffering off;` on the SSE location.
- Increase proxy_read_timeout and keepalive settings so proxy doesn't time out upstream streams.
- Ensure TLS offload doesn't rebuffer large chunks (some ALBs do).

eng_lucy: On the Redwood runtime side we can also: reduce maximum single-chunk sends (stream chunk size) so we push smaller writes that are less likely to fill socket buffer; increase per-socket write deadline from 15s -> 30s for streaming; and add exponential backoff+retry logic when write returns EAGAIN instead of aborting immediately. 

support_julia: Customer also worried about double-billing. Why are they billed twice?

eng_lucy: Current billing is per-completed-response tokens. If client reconnects and we start a new generation, it's a new request id and new billing. We have a couple options: idempotency keys (server can detect restart attempts and either resume or skip re-execution) or server-side check to mark partial completions (issue credit). Short-term: recommend client uses idempotency_token and `X-Resume-If-Exists` header (not yet GA) — we'll file follow-up.

customer_tom: We don't control all clients; many are thin browsers. For now we just need reliability. We'll try the nginx changes. Anything we should change on our side?

sre_matt: Client-side: implement EventSource reconnect jitter, but more important is consuming the stream as quickly as possible. If you can't, try increasing socket buffer on your edge nodes (SO_RCVBUF) and turn off proxy buffering.

deploy-bot: deploy:promote v1.42.3 -> prod at 1780001300 by eng-lucy :rocket:

eng_lucy: I'll patch runtime in v1.42.4 to: 1) add smaller chunking for streaming; 2) extend stream_write_timeout_ms default to 30s; 3) add debug metric for write-block occurrences (counter: stream.write_eagain). Will schedule rollout to dedicated and hosted.

support_julia: Action items summary:
- customer_tom: disable nginx proxy_buffering on SSE endpoints and increase proxy_read_timeout (SOX) — please confirm after test.
- eng_lucy: send PR for smaller chunking + increase write timeout + write_eagain metric (owner: lucy).
- sre_matt: add runbook snippet for EAGAIN/backpressure (include kernel buffers, proxy buffering, client slowness).
- billing: create follow-up ticket to explore idempotency/resume to prevent duplicate charges (assigned: bill_team).

customer_tom: Will try nginx change now and report. If we still see drops I'll paste tcpdump + timeline. Thanks all. :headphones:

sre_matt: One more debug tip: on the runtime host run `ss -t -o state established '( sport = :443 )'` to inspect timer info and `cat /proc/net/sockstat` for buffer usage. Also capture `strace -e write -p <pid>` for a few seconds to see EAGAINs.

eng_lucy: I'll monitor the new metric and correlate with customer request ids; if we see lots of stream.write_eagain we'll consider server-side buffered queuing to smooth bursts.

support_julia: Thanks everyone — marking this thread for follow-up.
